dimensions.reasons: The designated final image, rain_lily_macro_final.png, clearly depicts a single centered open white six-tepal rain-lily-like flower, green throat, exposed yellow anthers, pale central style, surrounding strap leaves, and brown litter. Its high, slightly oblique macro framing is broadly consistent with the reference.
issues: The scene reads as a simplified studio-style 3D diorama rather than a close natural ground photograph.
The finite smooth brown ground slab and sparse, geometric tan debris differ substantially from the dense, irregular organic leaf-and-stem litter in the reference.
The flower is much more symmetrical, flatter, and more uniformly arranged than the natural reference bloom.

dimensions.reasons: In cam_submitted.png and the Group A overview views, petals meet coherently at the throat, filaments visibly emerge from the center, and the leaves, dried leaf pieces, and wood-chip-like pieces appear layered on the ground plane. No clear floating object or severe collision is visible.
issues: The flower lacks a clearly visible supporting stem/base, so it reads somewhat like a bloom placed directly among the litter.
Several debris pieces are very flat and schematic, reducing the sense of naturally settled organic material.

dimensions.reasons: The primary forms are independently readable in rain_lily_macro_final.png: six white pointed petals, a yellow-green center, white filaments, saturated yellow oval anthers, a forked pale style, green strap leaves, and brown ground debris. Preview7 also makes the faint longitudinal petal lines visible.
issues: The petals are overly smooth, broad, and evenly icon-like rather than subtly irregular, tapered natural tepals.
The throat is an intense lime-green glow rather than the more localized natural green fade in the reference.
Leaves are overly saturated bright green with a plastic-looking highlight.
The litter is composed largely of clean tan cutout leaves and rectangular sticks rather than varied dried foliage, stems, and wood chips.

dimensions.reasons: The final macro render has a coherent shallow-depth-of-field look and recognizable floral anatomy, but its regular petal geometry, smooth surfaces, highly uniform colors, and simplified debris make it visibly synthetic. The reference is a natural macro photograph with much richer organic variation.
issues: Petal, leaf, and litter materials do not provide convincing fine natural surface variation.
The green throat looks softly emissive/airbrushed rather than like a physically lit floral interior.
The simplified brown slab and cleanly separated debris undermine the illusion of a real forest-floor or garden-bed setting.
The early preview exports are severely overexposed, although the final export itself is substantially more usable.

dimensions.reasons: rain_lily_macro_final.png places the bloom prominently in the center with long green leaves crossing beneath and behind it and brown litter around it, matching the principal spatial relationships of the reference. The reproductive structures are unobstructed as requested.
issues: The leaves radiate in a more deliberate spoke-like arrangement than the looser, partially occluded leaf placement in the reference.
The surrounding ground cover is too sparse and evenly distributed.
The rendered bloom fills more of the frame and is more frontally centered than the reference's slightly more natural off-axis presentation.

dimensions.reasons: The flower-to-leaf scale is generally sensible and the six petals have a plausible radial bloom footprint. The anthers and style are clearly legible at macro scale.
issues: The green throat is disproportionately broad and visually dominant relative to the petal bases.
The bright yellow anthers are noticeably thick, large, and uniformly oval compared with the small yellow-orange anthers in the reference.
The scattered chips and dried leaves look oversized and stylized relative to the bloom.

dimensions.reasons: The final image uses soft light and depth-of-field effectively enough to keep the flower center visible while softening surrounding leaves and litter. Faint petal vein lines are supported by rain_lily_preview7.png.
issues: The white petals are close to featureless bright white in much of rain_lily_macro_final.png, with limited visible waxiness, translucency, or subtle SSS response.
Veins are faint and overly uniform rather than fine natural longitudinal texture.
The throat transition is too bright and diffuse, while leaf and litter materials lack the requested roughness, mottling, and organic texture variation.
The material treatment is cleaner and more plasticky than the softly natural daylight appearance of the target photo.

dimensions.reasons: All core requested visible components are present in the final render: one six-petal white bloom, green-to-white throat region, a cluster of white filaments with yellow anthers, a higher pale forked style, several long green leaves, and surrounding brown leaf/chip debris.
issues: The required ground-litter category is present but simplified; it lacks the dense variety of dried leaves, stems, muted vegetation, and irregular wood fragments visible in the reference.
Petal vein and material detail are present only weakly rather than clearly enough for a high-fidelity instructional botanical rendering.

criteria.criterion: The principal flower must form a complete six-tepal body with the required shape, venation, and material response.
The flower throat must use an authored spatial gradient that produces a clearly readable yellow-green-to-white instructional color transition.
The complete stamen, anther, and pistil system must have the specified identities, arrangement, material response, and unobstructed instructional visibility.
The surrounding living leaves must combine the requested form, distribution, direction, color, and surface response.
criteria.evidence: Several long, tapered green blade leaves radiate beneath and behind the bloom, including strong diagonal runs across the lower-left, upper-left, right, and lower-right of the frame. Their smooth green surfaces carry narrow soft highlights rather than a metallic reflection.

criteria.criterion: Dry fallen leaves and wood chips must jointly form a substantial, materially varied organic ground bed.
The authored key and environmental fill must work together to produce soft natural daylight and photographic shadows.
The final image must combine the requested elevated-oblique macro view, shallow focus, subject hierarchy, and broad reference character.
criteria.evidence: The designated author final image, rain_lily_macro_final, uses a close elevated, mildly tilted view with the six-petaled flower occupying most of the image. The flower center, yellow anthers, pale forked pistil, and green throat are clear, while the peripheral brown litter and rear green leaves are visibly softened by shallow focus. It retains the requested dominant white flower, diagonal blades, and warm brown litter hierarchy.

criteria.criterion: The completed vignette must maintain plausible biological scale, avoid invented modeled structures and unrelated objects, and integrate into a coherent instructional scene.
criteria.evidence: Although the floral structures are recognizable, the scene reads as a simplified staged model rather than an integrated natural vignette: Group A overview views clearly reveal a thin, finite square brown ground slab isolated in a large empty dark-blue field, and the surrounding litter consists largely of featureless rectangular strips and flat cutout-like tan fragments. This artificial support/staging conflicts with the reference's continuous natural ground vegetation and organic debris context.

criteria.criterion: The editable Blender project must correspond to the final scene, preserve the required authored render configuration, produce a clean result, and use organized naming.
The designated final image must be a valid authored PNG at the required effective resolution.

notes: The submission successfully models a recognizable six-petaled rain-lily-like flower with visible anthers, style, leaves, and debris, and its final macro composition broadly follows the target. Its major limitation is fidelity: the result is a clean, highly symmetrical, plastic-like 3D diorama on a finite brown slab rather than a convincing natural macro flower scene with richly varied botanical and ground-cover detail.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
